Title: Denmark sends conscripts to Greenland as Arctic tensions grow
Article:
KANGERLUSSUAQ: For the first time in recent history, Danish conscripts have been deployed to Greenland, as Denmark moves to bolster its presence in the Arctic after US demands to acquire the territory.
US President Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to acquire the semi-autonomous Danish island, citing national security concerns and accusing Copenhagen of neglecting Arctic defence.
Denmark and Greenland have firmly rejected the idea.
The conscripts are part of the first cohort under Denmark's new extended conscription programme, aimed at producing soldiers able to operate in one of the kingdom's most strategically important and challenging regions.
"It shows presence that we're here and not just thinking of our own skin. And also thinking of the people in Greenland," 19-year-old conscript David told Reuters.
Copenhagen has pledged billions of dollars to strengthen Arctic defences after Denmark's defence minister acknowledged years of underinvestment in the region.
"Of course, we are a part of a bigger picture of the strategic communication about Greenland, but our role here is just to continue the training of the conscripts, the soldiers, and get more experience with the training in the Arctic terrain and climate," company commander Captain Laura Jepsen said.
The conscripts are taking part in Arctic Endurance, a Danish military exercise that trains soldiers for combat and survival in extreme cold-weather conditions.
The drill forms part of Arctic Sentry, a Nato mission launched this year to strengthen the alliance's Arctic presence and ease tensions within Nato after Trump's remarks about Greenland.
Russia, which maintains the Arctic's largest military footprint, has criticised Nato's growing activity in the region, describing it as a direct security threat that increases the risk of confrontation.
China has increased its activity in the mineral-rich region, mostly in partnership with Moscow.
Training north of the Arctic Circle, the conscripts moved through a landscape of bare rock and open expanses with no trees in sight.
"I think it sends a message that Denmark is reinforcing itself for the future," Anton, 22, one of the conscripts, said.

Title: Steel Hawk earnings visibility cloudy despite RM576mil tender book
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Steel Hawk Bhd's orderbook visibility remains limited in the near term despite its sizeable tender pipeline, as the company remains cautious about the oil and gas (O&G) environment.
TA Securities said Steel Hawk's current orderbook of RM63.4 million provides some revenue visibility going into the second half of the year (2H FY26), but remains relatively modest compared with its RM575.8 million tender book.
Notably, 76.1 per cent of the current orderbook and 77.9 per cent of the tender book comprise non-O&G projects, reflecting the group's ongoing diversification into power and utilities, infrastructure, data centres and healthcare.
"While this broadens Steel Hawk's addressable market, a meaningful portion of the potential growth remains dependent on securing new awards, with management guiding to only 10–20 per cent conversion of the tender book. We therefore remain cautious on the visibility of earnings beyond 2H FY26," it said in a note.
Steel Hawk also expects its third-quarter earnings to at least break even, with profitability in the fourth quarter of FY26 supported by the current orderbook scheduled for execution over the next three to four months.
"However, we remain cautious on the pace of recovery, given the sharp decline in 1H FY26 gross profit margin to 10.4 per cent from 41.2 per cent in 1H FY25. Lower work-order utilisation, higher raw material costs and SST absorption have weighed heavily on margins, while management's recovery assumptions remain dependent on tighter cost control and timely project execution," it added.
Steel Hawk also remains cautious about the near-term O&G environment, with work-order activity still subdued and competition intensifying as contractors vie for a limited pool of projects.
While the completion of Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) manpower rationalisation could support a gradual recovery in activity, several construction and modification work tenders have been delayed until late September or early October, limiting near-term visibility.
Moreover, the ongoing transition of Petronas Carigali contracts to Searah Ltd, a 50:50 joint venture between Petronas and Eni, has disrupted three of Steel Hawk's O&G contracts.
"We therefore see limited evidence of a meaningful O&G work-order recovery at this stage, with the timing of new awards remaining a key uncertainty," TA Securities said.
The research house maintained its "Sell" call on Steel Hawk with an unchanged target price of 10 sen, based on six times its FY27 earnings per share.

Title: Nepal tunnel rescuers seek trapped workers but hit dead ends
Article:
KATHMANDU: Nepali rescuers searched Wednesday for survivors feared trapped inside hydropower tunnels a week after devastating floods, but hopes were fading as teams hit dead ends and no one was confirmed alive.
The government had said intially it believed that more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels.
"The search and rescue operation is still underway, and foreign teams are also supporting it at the hydropower tunnels," said Shanti Mahat, spokeswoman of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).
"They are continuing to work despite difficulties. There is a heavy volume of mud and debris and sludge."
Those feared trapped are among 639 hydropower workers missing since a wall of mud and debris swept down on Aug 26, according to NDRRMA figures.
"In some cases it has been difficult to find the entry points and, even when they have been found, the rescuers have found the tunnels blocked inside," Mahat told AFP. "But efforts continue."
Rescuers pulled at least three bodies out of two tunnels on Monday, and entered several hundred metres into some tunnels, but were stopped by mud.
"We have access to all the tunnels, but it's problematic to get inside, as there are rocks and sludge," Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha told reporters on Tuesday.
The Nepal Electricity Authority said 11 hydropower stations and one solar power station, with a combined capacity of 431.1 megawatts, had stopped operating, about 10 per cent of the country's installed electricity generation capacity.
Another 15 power projects under construction, with a planned capacity of 470 megawatts, were damaged.

Title: Bangladeshi minister's 200,000-worker claim not official govt position – Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A Bangladeshi minister's claim that Malaysia plans to recruit 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over the next six months does not represent the official position of the Bangladeshi government, says government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan had informed him that the statement was made by a junior minister and should not be regarded as an official declaration by the Bangladeshi government.
"It does not represent the official decision of the Bangladeshi government. That is what the Human Resources Minister informed me. So, it is not an official position," he told reporters during his weekly press conference here.
Yesterday, Bangladeshi Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Junior Minister Mir Shahe Alam said Malaysia
planned
to recruit about 200,000 Bangladeshi workers over the next six months.
He said the workers would be recruited through companies approved by Malaysian authorities, with recruitment beginning in phases at the end of September and completed within six months.
In June, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to
consider
reopening Malaysia's labour market to Bangladeshi workers.
Malaysia restricted the recruitment of Bangladeshi workers in 2024 following reports of exploitation, including debt bondage, forced labour and workers arriving without the jobs promised to them.
The reported intake comes as Putrajaya seeks to
reduce
its reliance on foreign labour, with the government targeting a reduction in foreign workers to about 10 per cent of the total workforce by 2030.
The NST is seeking further clarification from Ramanan.

Title: 'Saint Seiya' anime author claims former aide embezzled US$29m
Article:
TOKYO: The Japanese author of globally popular manga series "Saint Seiya", Masami Kurumada, said Wednesday he was suing a former business associate for allegedly embezzling US$29 million.
Kurumada, 72, said the former manager responsible for the accounting of the artist's businesses siphoned off the sum over more than 10 years.
"I trusted this man with all of our monetary inflows and outflows. But he had been embezzling (from the firms) for over a decade," Kurumada told a news conference in Tokyo.
"You hear about these types of embezzlement crimes in the news. Yet I myself, in my over-50-year career, have never encountered a bad man like this in the world of anime and comic books. I couldn't believe it. I was like, 'Why?'"
The former manager has returned 1.8 billion yen (US$11.3 million) of the 4.68 billion yen he is alleged to have embezzled, according to local media.
Kurumada has filed a damage claim with the Tokyo District Court against the former staff member and his businesses to recover the remaining 2.89 billion yen, local media said.
The author reportedly said that his business, Kurumada Production, "could have gone bankrupt" and that the company's accounts had limited funds when the embezzlement was discovered, "making it impossible to pay significant taxes".
Kurumada began writing "Saint Seiya" in the 1980s for the weekly Shonen Jump, an influential manga publication that has produced global hits such as "One Piece", "Dragon Ball" and "Naruto".
"Saint Seiya" has sold more than 50 million copies worldwide, according to specialist site Mangazenkan.
Drawing heavily on Greek mythology, it has been adapted into an animated series, animated films, video games and trading cards.

Title: Fomca advises public to limit outdoor activities amid haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A consumer watchdog has advised Malaysians to limit outdoor activities and strenuous exercise when air quality reaches unhealthy levels amid continuing haze.
"Haze is not merely about poor visibility. It is about the quality of the air that millions of people breathe every day," the Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) chief executive officer Dr T. Saravanan told the New Straits Times.
Saravanan said schools, childcare centres and organisers of outdoor programmes should follow official advisories and place health and safety ahead of planned activities.
"Employers also have a responsibility to protect workers," he said, calling for appropriate protection and reasonable work adjustments for construction workers, delivery riders, security personnel, cleaners and others who spent long hours outdoors.
"Fomca's message to Malaysians is simple: monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API), reduce your exposure, protect vulnerable family members and be prepared for the possibility that the haze may continue for some time."
Haze has affected many parts of the country since early August, particularly Sarawak, with transboundary smoke from
forest and peatland fires in Indonesia
contributing to deteriorating air quality.

Title: Jakim backs decision over 'Madu atau Racun', lodges report with MCMC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Islamic Development Department (Jakim) has backed the decision by the Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) to reject the airing of
Madu atau Racun
, a drama series.
Jakim said the decision was justified as the drama, which is available on the iQIYI platform, featured elements that contradicted religious and cultural values, sparking public concern.
"The issue was closely monitored based on the Guidelines for the Screening of Islamic Content in Broadcasting Materials (Jakim Bil. 4/2015)," it said.
Jakim has lodged a report with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC).
The department will cooperate with relevant agencies, including MCMC and the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas), to ensure necessary action is taken in accordance with the law.
The
Communications and Multimedia Content Forum Malaysia
(CMCF) will meet the producers of the controversial drama series and iQIYI representatives.

Title: [UPDATED] Former TH COO Adi Azuan expected to be charged tomorrow
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief operating officer Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani is expected to be charged at the Sessions Court here tomorrow.
According to the court's cause list, Adi Azuan is scheduled to appear before judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud at 9am.
The nature of the charge was not stated in the court listing.
Adi Azuan joined TH in July 2002 as its group accounts divisional head before later becoming its chief operating officer.
Adi Azuan was previously among five senior TH officials named in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report, which found that disciplinary action imposed on them for several cases of serious misconduct was later reduced following appeals.
The four others were former group chief financial officer Datuk Rozaida Omar, former senior general manager of corporate services and property Rifina Md Ariff, former chief human resources officer Mohd Hisham Harun and former legal adviser Hazlina Mohd Khalid.
According to the RCI report, the disciplinary action involved four case clusters.
These were the sale of shares in PT TH Indo Plantations, non-compliance with the Companies Act 1965 over a RM22.12 million contribution to Yayasan Tabung Haji without prior ministerial approval, issues surrounding the 2017 hibah profit distribution declaration and the submission of false claims.
In the case involving the RM22.12 million contribution to Yayasan Tabung Haji, Adi Azuan, Rozaida and Hisham were initially demoted.
Following appeals, the penalties against Adi Azuan and Rozaida were reduced to stern warnings, while Hisham received a warning and a salary increment freeze.
The RCI also disclosed that several internal TH investigations had led to reports being lodged with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) over alleged misconduct and abuse of power.
Among the matters referred to the MACC were alleged corruption involving TH Plantation's acquisition of Weida Bhd plantations, as well as alleged abuse of power and irregularities in the leasing of Restoran Opah at KL Sentral and Restoran Nasi Dalca at TH's headquarters.

Title: Iran's top negotiator calls US 'Satan' after wedding attack
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf on Wednesday called the United States "Satan" after an attack on a wedding ceremony in the country's south.
At least four people were killed and dozens wounded in a late-night strike on the ceremony in Kuhestak in southern Iran, according to Iranian officials.
Ghalibaf said the attack left "children killed with families", while singling out several deadly incidents in Iran during the initial stages of the Middle East war, including an attack on a school in Minab.
"If a power acts like Satan, picks targets like Satan, and kills like Satan, it's Satan.
"Shields a junior Satan that does the same? It's THE Great Satan," said Ghalibaf in a post on X, referring to the US and key ally Israel.
The 'Satan' term was originally coined by Ruhollah Khomeini, founder of the Islamic Republic, in 1979 and has since been used by successive Iranian leaders to refer to the United States.
Iran responded to the wedding attack by launching drone and missile attacks on US bases across the Middle East, including in Bahrain, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Iraq's Kurdistan region.
The US military did not address the wedding strike directly.
US Central Command (CENTCOM) spokesman Tim Hawkins said "the US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC", referring to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.

Title: More than 2,000 PBM members quit to join Wawasan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 2,000 Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM) members announced their decision to join Parti Wawasan Negara today.
Former PBM national youth chief Hanis Asmui said the move followed the dissolution of the party's central, state, and division youth committees effective immediately today.
He said the decision was made unanimously, voluntarily, and without coercion or pressure from any party.
"We took into account the fact that confidence in the party's top leadership has eroded and can no longer be restored.
"The main trigger for this issue is PBM national information chief Ronnie Liu, who frequently makes superficial statements regarding religion, royalty, and race (3R)," he said at a press conference at Plaza Conlay here today.
It was previously reported that Liu announced his decision to join PBM after 41 years in DAP, where he served several terms as a Central Executive Committee (CEC) member.
PBM is led by president Datuk Larry Sng, while Wawasan is led by president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
Hanis said the decision to leave the party had been considered over the past three months after internal conflicts could no longer be resolved.
"It is expected that more PBM members will leave the party, including from the women's wing.
"We view the existing leadership as no longer reflecting the true aspirations of grassroots members.
"Furthermore, they have failed to demonstrate a serious commitment to the comprehensive reforms urgently needed now," he said.
He said Wawasan was seen as a major platform to stabilise national politics, unify Malay political parties such as Pas and Umno, and bridge racial divides.
"We are confident in Hamzah's leadership to bring change to the country's political landscape," he said.

Title: High Court dismisses Malaysian Bar bid to challenge HRD Corp levy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has dismissed the Malaysian Bar's judicial review challenging the application of the Human Resources Development Corporation (HRD Corp) levy and training framework to the legal profession.
Judge Alice Loke ruled that there was no conflict between the Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 (PSMB Act) and the Legal Profession Act 1976 (LPA).
She said the PSMB Act complemented the Malaysian Bar's role in providing training to members of the legal profession by allocating a specific fund for that purpose.
"The applicant (Malaysian Bar) is also not precluded or prohibited from conducting its own training programmes.
"I therefore fail to see a conflict or inconsistency between the PSMB Act and the LPA," she said in her grounds of judgment dated Aug 28.
Loke said there was no basis to invoke the legal principle that a specific law should prevail over a general law.
The case arose following the Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Bhd (Amendment of First Schedule) Order 2021, issued by the human resources minister on Feb 26, 2021.
The order, which came into force on March 1 that year, expanded the industries covered by the PSMB Act to more than 40 sectors, including the professional industry, which cover the legal profession.
Under the act, employers in industries covered by the legislation are required to register with HRD Corp and pay a human resources development levy.
Employers with 10 or more Malaysian employees are required to contribute one per cent of their employees' monthly wages, with the funds available to finance employee training.
The Malaysian Bar argued that the 2021 order encroached on the LPA and overlapped with its Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Scheme.
It contended that the legal profession was already governed by the LPA, under which the Bar was responsible for maintaining and improving professional standards and learning among lawyers.
It also argued that requiring law firms to contribute to the HRD Fund could affect income generated from the Bar's CPD programmes.
However, Loke said HRD Corp essentially acted as the trustee and manager of the HRD Fund by registering employers and training providers, collecting levies and disbursing funds for training.
"PSMB does not conduct any training," she said, adding that training was conducted by registered providers based on their own courses and programmes.
The judge noted that the Malaysian Bar itself had been registered as a training provider under the PSMB Act between 2016 and 2023 and had conducted HRD Fund-claimable training under its CPD Scheme.
Loke also rejected the Bar's argument that Section 49 of the PSMB Act, which empowers the minister to amend the First Schedule, amounted to excessive delegation of Parliament's legislative power.
She said the Bar continued to retain control over its own training programmes, which remained independent of the PSMB Act.
The judge also rejected the Bar's reliance on the auditor general's and Public Accounts Committee reports concerning HRD Corp.
She added that the matters raised in the reports were also not part of the Bar's pleaded grounds for judicial review.

Title: Khazanah delegation visits Media Prima headquarters
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Khazanah Nasional Berhad managing director Datuk Amirul Feisal Wan Zahir today led a delegation on a corporate visit to Balai Berita, the headquarters of Media Prima Berhad, to strengthen engagement and gain an insight into the group's media, news, digital and content operations.
The visit also provided an opportunity for senior representatives from both organisations to exchange views on Media Prima's business and strategic direction, as well as its evolving media and digital ecosystem.
The delegation was welcomed by Media Prima group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali, Media Prima Content and TV Networks and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof, Media Prima News and Current Affairs group managing editor Jasbant Singh, and Media Prima News and Current Affairs deputy group managing editor and New Straits Times group editor Datuk Farrah Naz Karim.
Also accompanying Amirul Feisal were Khazanah's head of Group Sustainability and Advocacy Datuk Shahira Ahmad Bazeri and chief corporate officer and gheneral counsel Mohamed Nasri Sallehuddin, along with other Khazanah officials.
The delegation toured Media Prima Audio, the News & Current Affairs studios, WHI studio, Rev Media Group and the editorial floor housing KLIK, where they were briefed on the group's operations across broadcasting, news, digital media and content production.
The visit also included a lighter moment when Amirul Feisal tried his hand at newsreading in front of the camera for tonight's TV3 news slot.
The delegation later adjourned to the Boardroom before the visit ended at about 3pm.

Title: High Court rejects citizenship bid by woman born out of wedlock to Malaysian father
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Muar High Court has dismissed a woman's bid for Malaysian citizenship by operation of law despite her biological father being a Malaysian citizen.
Judicial commissioner Kalyana Kumar Sockalingam said the woman was not entitled to citizenship as she was born out of wedlock to a Malaysian father and an Indonesian mother.
The court heard that her parents were not lawfully married at the time of her birth and her birth records were subsequently amended to classify her as a non-citizen.
Kalyana said the court was bound by the Federal Court's ruling, which had authoritatively settled the constitutional interpretation governing citizenship for children born out of wedlock.
"The applicant's biological father is undoubtedly a Malaysian citizen. However, that fact alone does not determine the constitutional position.
"The majority decision of the Federal Court authoritatively settled that by virtue of Article 31, Section 17 of Part III forms part of the interpretative framework governing Article 14(1)(b) of the Federal Constitution.
"Consequently, where a child is born illegitimate, every constitutional reference to 'father' or 'parent' must be construed as referring to the mother.
"That interpretation binds this court under the doctrine of stare decisis, and this court has no jurisdiction to adopt a contrary construction.
"Since the applicant's mother is an Indonesian citizen, the constitutional requirements for citizenship by operation of law under Article 14(1)(b) are not fulfilled," he said in his grounds of judgment published by the Judiciary Department today.
The court also rejected the applicant's reliance on Section 19B of the Constitution, which concerns newborn children found abandoned and provides certain presumptions concerning their birth and parentage.
Kalyana said the provision was intended to deal with cases where the parentage of an abandoned newborn was unknown or incapable of being proven.
"In the present case, the biological father of the applicant has been identified. More importantly, the biological mother has also been identified as an Indonesian national," he said.
The court also rejected the woman's contention that the decision to classify her as a non-citizen contravened Articles 5 and 8 of the Constitution, concerning personal liberty and equality.
"Articles 5 and 8 of the Federal Constitution are general guarantees of equality and personal liberty. However, citizenship is specifically governed by Part III of the Constitution.
"It is a settled principle of constitutional interpretation that a specific constitutional provision prevails over general guarantees.
"As such, there is no contravention of Articles 5 and 8 of the Constitution in the present case," he said.
The court acknowledged the woman's predicament but said it could not depart from the constitutional interpretation laid down by the Federal Court.
"The applicant's grievance is understandable. Nevertheless, courts are bound to apply the Constitution as interpreted by the Federal Court.
"Any change to this constitutional framework lies with parliament through constitutional amendment rather than judicial innovation," he added.
The court made no order as to costs.
Senior federal counsel Norafiah Saini acted for the government while lawyer Alvin Chang represented the applicant.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1,476 Myanmar refugees signed documents for voluntary repatriation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The 1,476 Myanmar refugees set to be repatriated at the end of this month have signed documents stating that they voluntarily wish to return, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Fahmi said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had briefed the cabinet on the matter, explaining that the figure was determined through a screening process involving more than 10,000 Myanmar refugees held at immigration detention depots.
"5,000 names were (then) screened by the Home Ministry, and these 5,000 names were then forwarded to the Myanmar embassy.
"From that list, 1,476 have been agreed upon by Myanmar to be received back, and this will take place at the end of September," he said during a weekly press conference here.

Title: Federal Court grants govt, police leave to appeal death-in-custody rulings
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Federal Court here today granted the government and police leave to appeal against a ruling that held them liable for the death of gravedigger Mohd Fadzrin Zaidi, who was found hanging in a police lock-up in 2019.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Nordin Hassan, Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and Datuk Azmi Ariffin allowed the application on two questions of law.
The first question concerns the principles governing the imposition of a duty of care. The second pertains to whether the nature of the criminal offence committed by a detainee is a factor that the court is required to take into consideration when applying the principle of reasonable foreseeability in cases of detainee suicide.
The same panel also granted leave to appeal in a separate case brought by the family of security guard M. Thinagaran, who had sued the government and two other parties for negligence over his death.
The two questions of law raised in Thinagaran's case were similar to those posed in Fadzrin's case.
In Fadzrin's case, the government and police sought leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal's decision of Jan 26 this year, which had affirmed the High Court's ruling holding them liable for his death.
Fadzrin, 29, was arrested during a drug raid on Nov 20, 2019, and remanded for seven days. He was detained at the Seberang Perai Utara District Police Headquarters lock-up and was found hanged in his cell in the early hours of the following day.
His mother, Fadhelah Othman, commenced proceedings against the police and the government at the Georgetown High Court in 2022.
In May 2024, the High Court found the police negligent in failing to prevent Mohd Fadzrin from taking his own life while in custody.
The court also held the government vicariously liable for that negligence and awarded Fadhelah RM147,600 in damages.
The Court of Appeal upheld the finding of liability but reduced the damages to RM97,600, comprising RM57,600 for loss of dependency, RM30,000 for pain and suffering, and RM10,000 in special damages.
It also set aside the award of RM50,000 in aggravated damages.
In Thinagaran's case, his widow, R. Tenaswari, and his father, K. Madhavan, as joint administrators of his estate, brought an action against the government, the Selangor maritime director, and a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) investigating officer, claiming negligence, breach of statutory duty and misfeasance in public office.
Thinagaran, 31, was found dead in 2019 while detained at the MMEA lock-up in Klang, having hanged himself from the ceiling of his cell using a pair of pants provided to him.
The High Court allowed the negligence claim and awarded RM172,800 for loss of earnings, RM6,370 in special damages, RM5,000 for funeral expenses and RM10,000 for bereavement.
However, the Court of Appeal overturned that decision, prompting his family to seek leave to appeal to the Federal Court.
At the Federal Court today, senior federal counsels Zureen Elina Mohd Dom and Nur Ezdiani Roleb appeared for the government and police.
Lawyers M. Visvanathan, V. Sanjay Nathan and Pushan Qin Nathan represented Fadhelah.
In Thinagaran's case, lawyer M. Manoharan represented the family, while senior federal counsel Liew Horng Bin and Siti Syakimah Ibrahim appeared for the government.

Title: [UPDATED]: CMCF to meet 'Madu atau Racun' producers, iQIYI over controversial content
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Communications and Multimedia Content Forum Malaysia (CMCF) will meet the producers of controversial drama series 'Madu atau Racun' and streaming platform iQIYI to obtain a comprehensive explanation regarding its content.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the government has made the directive and it would not compromise with any production party that touched on religious and racial sensitivities.
The series drew public outcry over alleged lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ+) themes.
"The government wishes to emphasise that we will not compromise with any production party that touches on religious and racial sensitivities in their work.
"Creative freedom must be accompanied and balanced with the responsibility to respect religious values, social harmony, and racial and cultural sensitivities that form the foundation and pillar of our national unity," he told reporters during a weekly press conference.
Fahmi explained that National Film Development Corporation (Finas) had regulatory jurisdiction over film activities and cinema screenings, while the Malaysian Communication and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) regulated television broadcasting and communications.
However, he said, over-the-top (OTT) streaming platforms via the internet were not yet fully subject to the same licensing framework.
"Although content on OTT platforms is currently not directly subject to Finas licensing oversight, the ministry has directed the CMCF to hold a meeting this afternoon with the production house and iQIYI to obtain a comprehensive explanation regarding the drama's content," he added.
He said the government would not hesitate to take appropriate action if the investigation found any violation of applicable guidelines, regulations or determinations.
He said Finas would issue a statement on the meeting's outcome.
Earlier today, Finas chief executive officer Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib said the body lacks legal authority to take down 'Madu Atau Racun' from streaming platforms.
He clarified that its enforcement reach is bound by existing legal parameters, which currently apply to cinema releases rather than OTT streaming services regulated outside the Film Censorship Board.
Starring Aliff Aziz, Uqasha Senrose, and Elisya Sandha, 'Madu Atau Racun' recently drew sharp criticism from viewers who deemed its scenes inappropriate for local audiences, prompting widespread calls for the series to be pulled.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 77 Malaysians found safe in Tibet, Nepal being repatriated
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The 77 Malaysians found safe in Tibet and Nepal following last week's flash floods are being brought to Kathmandu for repatriation to Malaysia, said government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, adding that 55 Malaysians have yet to be traced.
"The Foreign Minister (Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan) has also informed the cabinet that there are 55 Malaysian citizens who have yet to be traced.
"Meanwhile, 77 Malaysians have been located in Tibet and Nepal. They have been brought to Kathmandu for repatriation to Malaysia," he told reporters during a weekly press conference here.
Fahmi said the cabinet took note of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's approval of a US$1 million contribution towards humanitarian efforts.
On Aug 30, Anwar also announced the
deployment of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team
(SMART) to Nepal to assist in search and rescue operations.
The flash floods struck the Nepal-Tibet border area on Aug 26, triggered by what is believed to have been a rock avalanche in the Himalayas.
On Monday, the number of missing people soared to nearly 4,500, while the confirmed
death toll
rose to more than 900, with unidentified bodies buried in mass graves after DNA sampling.
Malaysians were among the nationalities listed by Nepal's tourism board as foreign tourists still out of communication, alongside nationals from India, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, Canada, Latvia and several other countries.

Title: Boat operator arrested, remanded four days over Mersing collision
Article:
MERSING: A 33-year-old boat operator was remanded for four days from today to assist investigations into a collision involving two passenger boats at Kuala Sungai Mersing on Monday.
The man, who was operating one of the boats involved in the incident, was arrested by a team from the district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Division about noon yesterday.
Police obtained the four-day remand order from the Kota Tinggi magistrate's court, with the remand order running from today until Sept 5 under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspect had a previous criminal record involving a drug offence.
However, he tested negative in an initial urine screening.
The case is being investigated under Section 304A of the Penal Code for causing death by negligence, which carries a maximum two-year jail term, a fine, or both upon conviction.
Police are also investigating the case under Section 280 of the Penal Code for negligently operating a vessel, which carries a maximum six-month jail term, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both upon conviction.
The investigation is being conducted in parallel with a sudden-death investigation, Rahaman said in a statement today.
On Aug 31, the Sea Queen, carrying six people, collided with the Rawa Birds, which had three people aboard, about 800m from the Sungai Mersing jetty.
The impact killed the 38-year-old Sea Queen skipper and a 32-year-old male passenger.
Seven others were injured, with three treated at Mersing Hospital, three at Sultan Ismail Hospital and one at Pasir Gudang Hospital.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Malaysia Day celebrations to be held indoors in Kuching amid haze
Article:
Malaysia Day celebrations on Sept 16 will be held indoors at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) due to worsening haze conditions in Sarawak, government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
"The cabinet also took note that the rather worrying haze conditions in Kuching and Sri Aman in Sarawak will result in outdoor events being unable to proceed, but the Malaysia Day celebration will be held indoors on the evening of Sept 16," the communications minister told reporters during his weekly press conference.
Meanwhile, on cloud seeding operations in Sarawak, Fahmi said the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry had informed the Cabinet that operations were subject to recommendations from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), based on the detection of clouds suitable for seeding.
He said the ministry had informed the Cabinet that several cloud formations recently detected had been found unsuitable, as wind movements had pushed them towards the South China Sea.
This, Fahmi added, meant any seeding conducted would not produce rainfall in the areas that needed it most.
"If cloud seeding were conducted, the rain would not fall in the areas where it is needed. The operation is therefore subject to the views and decisions of the Malaysian Meteorological Department," Fahmi said.
He also conveyed the prime minister's appreciation and congratulations to the entire team behind the National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31, which drew more than 100,000 attendees, with over 10,000 participating as part of contingents or the human graphic display.
Three areas in Sarawak recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today, with the Serian district police headquarters station recording the highest reading at 320.
Based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the other two areas with hazardous API readings were Kuching (318) and Samarahan (302).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Businessman loses safe, Mercedes in RM550,000 break-in
Article:
SUNGAI PETANI: A businessman suffered losses of about RM550,000 after his house in Taman Seri Jenaris, Tikam Batu, was broken into and a safe and his Mercedes were stolen early yesterday.
Kuala Muda police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan said the victim realised his house had been broken into when he returned home around noon.
Hanyan said the house was not equipped with closed-circuit television (CCTV), but police received information from members of the public who claimed to have seen three individuals suspected of being involved in the incident.
"No arrests have been made so far, but efforts to track down the suspects are ongoing," he said.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 457 of the Penal Code for housebreaking, while investigations were also ongoing into the vehicle theft.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man held for allegedly assaulting wife after she refused to give him gambling money
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A 35-year-old man was remanded for three days from today for allegedly assaulting his wife after she refused to give him money to gamble online.
Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno issued the remand order until Friday to allow police to complete their investigation under Section 323 of the Penal Code, read with Section 326A, for voluntarily causing hurt to a spouse.
The incident occurred at 4am on Aug 31 at a house in Rengit after the suspect allegedly became angry and struck the woman several times on the head, causing injuries.
The victim, who said she could no longer tolerate his hot-tempered behaviour and repeated assaults, lodged a report at the Rengit police station on the same day.
Police arrested the suspect at his home at 1.30pm yesterday to assist in investigations.
Preliminary investigations found that the suspect allegedly assaulted the woman after she refused to give him money for online gambling.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Missing Nepal climber's family gets support from Penang reps
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Bukit Gelugor member of parliament Ramkarpal Singh and Seri Delima assemblyman Connie Tan visited the family of missing climber Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, today.
Ramkarpal said the visit was to show solidarity and support for the family following the difficult situation they were facing.
"We understand the difficult situation the family is going through. I understand the victim was supposed to return last Monday, but unfortunately, this disaster occurred.
"I have also informed the family that we will provide any developments or updates received from Wisma Putra. I will seek the latest information so that we can provide full support to the family," he said after visiting Muhaimin's family at Taman Tun Sardon, Gelugor, here.
Ramkarpal contributed RM2,000 to the family, while Tan donated RM1,000.
Tan said they had also provided basic necessities to the family as one of its members has diabetes-related health issues.
"The Social Welfare Department will also visit this afternoon to provide psychological support to the family," she added.
Media reports previously said Muhaimin, Muhammad Adib Haikal Awang Mansor, 27, and Muhammad Zaki Othman, 29, could not be contacted while climbing in Langtang Valley, Nepal.
The trio are believed to have been in the area when flash floods and landslides hit the Nepal-Tibet border on Aug 26.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'We are distraught, worried about Muhaimin's fate in Nepal,' says father
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The family of missing Malaysian climber Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, remains distraught over his fate as the search for him continues in Nepal.
His father, Noor Hadi Mohd Hassan, 62, said the family was also worried by the lack of updates on the search and rescue (SAR) operation to locate Muhaimin and his two friends.
"We just want to know how our son is doing. If there is any development in the search operation, please tell us so we know what is happening there.
"If they have been out of contact for days, we do not know their condition, whether they have food or how they are surviving. That is what worries us. We fear their situation could get worse," he said when met at the family home in Taman Tun Sardon, Gelugor here today.
Noor Hadi said Muhaimin was a kind, cheerful and responsible son who played an important role in helping the family with various matters.
He said Muhaimin had also been helping him for more than 10 years after he became wheelchair-bound following the amputation of his right leg due to complications from diabetes.
"He takes me to the clinic, gets my hair cut and helps with various things. He is our hope.
"Muhaimin is our youngest child and he handles many family matters. When he is not around, it feels like we have lost a leg," he added.
Meanwhile, Muhaimin's mother, Zaleha Ariffin, 56, said her son had taken her shopping for household necessities before leaving and asked her to buy more than usual as he said he would be away longer this time.
"He also apologised to me before leaving. The last time we spoke was a day before the incident, when Muhaimin made a video call.
"As a mother, I can only pray and hope my son is found by the rescue team and returns safely to his family," she said tearfully.
Zaleha said Nepal was the first foreign country Muhaimin had visited for a climbing expedition.
She said Muhaimin had been interested in climbing since his student days and also enjoyed football and hockey.
It was reported that Muhaimin, Muhammad Adib Haikal Awang Mansor, 27, and Muhammad Zaki Othman, 29, could not be contacted while climbing in Langtang Valley, Nepal.
The trio are believed to have been in the area when flash floods and landslides hit the Nepal-Tibet border on Aug 26.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC urges Felda to appoint forensic audit team over governance issues
Article:
PUTRAJAYA:  The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has urged Felda to appoint its own forensic audit team to investigate governance weaknesses and misconduct within the agency.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said other enforcement agencies should also examine the weaknesses identified to ensure continuous efforts to prevent misconduct and embezzlement.
"We feel it is appropriate for Felda to appoint its own forensic audit team to conduct an audit on the issue.
"The team would have the authority to act on Felda's behalf and assist us in the investigation.
"For other investigative work, enforcement agencies besides MACC can also assist. The investigation is not being conducted by MACC alone," he said at a press conference here today.

Title: MACC reopens probe into seven Felda cases following new leads
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Seven Felda-related cases previously investigated or highlighted in forensic reports have been reopened after new information emerged, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the new leads provided grounds for the commission to re-examine the cases.
"Six cases that I announced involve new investigations, while one case involving Grand Park City is a continuation of a previous probe," he said.
The seven cases are:
1.Dataran Aras Sdn Bhd (DASB) – Felda purchased DASB in 2011 for RM148.2 million for an oil palm plantation project in Limbang, Sarawak, which faced major issues as the land could not be used.
2.Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd – The acquisition of the hotel in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, for RM86.4 million was investigated by MACC in 2017 to determine whether there were issues with the purchase method and overpayment, similar to hotel purchases in London and Kuching.
3.Merdeka Palace Hotel and Suites – The purchase of the hotel in Kuching, Sarawak, was among Felda Investment Corporation (FIC) property transactions investigated by MACC. The probe led to the prosecution of former Felda chairman Tan Sri Mohd Isa Abdul Samad on nine corruption charges involving RM3.09 million related to the RM160 million hotel purchase.
4.Park City Grand Plaza Kensington – The hotel property purchase in Kensington, London, was reopened by MACC in 2017 following new information, after an initial 2015 probe found no offences under the MACC Act.
5.Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd – The establishment and management of the biopharmaceutical firm were linked to governance weaknesses and dubious transactions identified in Felda's forensic review.
6.Felda House and Grand Felda House – The acquisition of two student accommodation properties in Wembley, London, was among FIC investments detailed in the Felda White Paper.
7.Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) – The development project on Felda land in Jalan Semarak, Kuala Lumpur, raised issues over land ownership transfer and project governance, though a 2018 MACC probe found no elements of corruption or abuse of power in the land transfer agreement.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 18 arrested, 11 remanded in Tabung Haji RCI probes
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A total of 18 people have been arrested and 245 witnesses called as the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigates 14 cases linked to the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said 11 of those arrested had been remanded in investigations involving allegations of corruption, misappropriation and abuse of power.
He said the 14 investigation papers comprised six cases directly referred to the MACC following the RCI report and another eight issues identified independently by the commission.
"Overall, through the 14 investigation papers opened by our special investigation team and Special Operations Division, 18 individuals have been arrested and 11 have been remanded," he said at a press conference here today.
Those arrested included a 61-year-old former managing director of Lembaga Tabung Haji (LTH), a 59-year-old director of Putrajaya Perdana and a 61-year-old former director of Putrajaya Perdana Construction Sdn Bhd.
Also arrested were a 60-year-old former chairman of LTH, a 69-year-old former director of Putrajaya Perdana Berhad and a 67-year-old chief operating officer of Alam Maritim Sdn Bhd.
The MACC also arrested a 65-year-old former senior general manager of LTH's Haj Division.
Two other individuals arrested were former senior general managers of LTH's Corporate, Finance and Services Division, aged 58 and 59 respectively.
Also among those detained was a 60-year-old former legal adviser to LTH.
Halim had earlier clarified that the arrests were made for investigation purposes and did not mean the individuals would immediately face charges.
He said 60 premises had also been entered and searched to obtain relevant documents for further investigations.
Of the six cases arising directly from the RCI referrals, two have been recommended for prosecution while four were classified as No Further Action (NFA).
Meanwhile, two of the eight additional investigation papers opened have been completed and submitted to the Attorney-General with recommendations for prosecution next week.
"If everything proceeds smoothly and the Attorney-General gives consent for prosecution, the cases will be registered in court next week," he said.
The remaining six additional cases are still ongoing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two arrested after newborn found in sanitary bin at Penang airport
Article:
BAYAN LEPAS: Police have arrested two people after a newborn baby boy was found alive inside a sanitary bin at Penang International Airport yesterday.
The two are a 23-year-old woman and a 22-year-old Myanmar man, who works as a security guard.
Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said the baby was discovered by a cleaner after the worker heard crying from
inside the bin at a toilet
for persons with disabilities.
"The baby was subsequently taken to Penang Hospital for treatment," he said in a statement today.
Anuwal said police investigations, including a review of closed-circuit television (CCTV) recordings, led to the woman's arrest at Kompleks Bukit Jambul.
"Further investigations led to the arrest of the Myanmar national, who was detained to assist with investigations.
"Police also found that the man had failed to produce valid travel documents," he added.
The baby is believed to have been delivered shortly before it was found, as the placenta and umbilical cord were still attached.
Forensic personnel from the Penang police headquarters also examined the scene, with several samples collected and sent to the Chemistry Department for analysis.
The case is being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code, relating to the abandonment of a child under 12 by a parent or person having care of the child.
Anuwal said investigations are ongoing to establish the involvement and links of those detained to the incident.
He urged the public not to speculate or circulate unverified information that could jeopardise police investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Strong waves raise beach danger as search continues for four teens
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Waves of more than a metre along Johor's east coast this week have raised drowning concerns as the school holidays draw more people to beaches for camping, picnics and swimming.
The warning comes as four 16-year-old boys remain missing after getting into difficulty while swimming at Tanjung Lompat beach in Tanjung Balau, Penawar, here, this morning.
Two others were
rescued by beachgoers
after they were spotted struggling in the water.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said rough seas, strong currents and increased recreational activity during the school break could heighten the risk of accidents.
She said fire stations near coastal areas had been ordered to step up monitoring, particularly during high tide and the transition between monsoons, when sea conditions can turn hazardous.
"Most drowning incidents occur during school holidays and camping activities at campsites along the coastal areas from Tanjung Balau to Desaru," she said.
Johor recorded seven beach drownings this year as of Sept 2, five of them in Kota Tinggi.
The state recorded 10 beach drownings in 2024 and 12 last year.
The latest incident came just three days after a father and son drowned while swimming at Kampung Punggai, Pengerang, on Aug 30.
Mohammad Nizam Zainal, 33, died while trying to save his eight-year-old son, Muhammad Zamri Mikhail, after both got into difficulty in rough seas during high tide.
Both were pulled from the water
but were pronounced dead
while receiving treatment at a nearby clinic.
In today's incident, the six boys got into difficulty while swimming at Tanjung Lompat beach.
Two were rescued by members of the public at 7.45am, while a search for the remaining four continued.
The missing boys were identified as Alif Taqiudin, Mohd Haiman, Adib Rizqi and Thaqif Rayyan.
Siti Rohani said the department had also taken preventive measures, including establishing the Water Activity Safety Council at Desaru public beach, Bandar Penawar, here, on Nov 10, 2019.
Since then, the department has conducted annual awareness campaigns to educate the public on the risks associated with beaches, rivers, lakes and other bodies of water.
She urged the public to stay out of the water during rough seas, strong waves or bad weather, warning that strong currents could sweep people away.
"Take heed of weather warnings and safety instructions issued by the authorities. A red flag means dangerous conditions and swimming is prohibited in the area," she said.
Siti Rohani also urged parents and guardians to closely supervise children and teenagers during the school holidays and ensure they swim only in designated areas with adequate safety facilities.
The search for the four missing teenagers was ongoing as of press time.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US encourages tourists to visit Sabah as security improves
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The United States is encouraging its citizens and visitors from around the world to travel to Sabah, following improvements in security and a more relaxed travel status for Borneo, said US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires to Malaysia David Gamble.
"Many countries are following America's lead and reviewing their travel advisories, which reflect the increased security and how safe it is to come to Sabah.
"We want to see more tourists from around the world come here because Sabah is a fantastic place to visit," he told reporters after launching the Freedom 250 campaign in Sabah at the state library in Tanjung Aru near here.
In February, the embassy lowered its travel advisory for Eastern Sabah to Level 1 for its citizens, advising them to exercise normal precautions, and Level 2 for the islands and maritime areas off the coast of Eastern Sabah.
Four months later, Japan also lowered its travel advisory for coastal areas from Kudat to Tawau from Level 2 to Level 1, covering Banggi Island and Balambangan Island.
The advisory had been raised in July 2014 following a series of kidnapping-for-ransom incidents involving foreigners on the east coast of Sabah.
Also present were Sabah Assistant Education, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Jordan Jude Ellron and US Assistant Secretary of State for Educational and Cultural Affairs Cate Dillon.
Freedom 250 Sabah is a three-day series of programmes taking place across Kota Kinabalu from yesterday until tomorrow to commemorate the 250th anniversary of American independence.
The celebration is organised in partnership with the Sabah state government, the City of Kota Kinabalu, local organisations and corporate sponsors.
During the three days, Tanjung Aru Library will host the travelling Freedom 250 Exhibition, Fulbright Malaysia and US higher education outreach, STEM workshops supported by McDermott and ConocoPhillips, English Access Scholarship Programme activities, and American Film Showcase workshops for emerging Sabahan filmmakers.
Prominent US athletes are leading the Freedom 250 Sabah Football Clinic Powered by ConocoPhillips, engaging up to 500 young Sabahan footballers.
Participating athletes include Shannon Boxx, a three-time Olympic gold medallist and Fifa Women's World Cup champion; Tony Sanneh, a veteran of the 2002 Fifa World Cup; and Maren Hendershot McCrary, a former professional football player.
Tomorrow, the celebration will culminate in the family-friendly "Great American Sabah State Fair" and the Freedom 250 Fun Run at Padang Merdeka from 3pm to 10pm, featuring American-style food, local vendors, contests, classic games and a live performance by the US Pacific Band, comprising Navy sailors from the US and partner countries.
The programme also features screenings of American classics, including Back to the Future, Mission: Impossible and The Incredibles, at City Cineplex, City Mall, celebrating American storytelling, creativity and technological innovation.
The Freedom 250 celebrations coincide with the 22nd Pacific Partnership mission in Sabah. Approximately 400 US service members and personnel from eight partner nations, including Australia, Japan and the United Kingdom, are working with local communities on engineering projects, medical outreach and disaster preparedness.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: OGX Group taps enterprise AI market with Axtraction tie-up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: OGX Group Bhd's wholly-owned unit, OGX Networks Sdn Bhd, has entered into a distribution agreement with Axtraction AI Sdn Bhd to market and distribute enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) solutions in Malaysia.
The agreement has an initial term of one year and may be renewed for successive three-year terms, subject to mutually agreed milestones being achieved.
"This partnership is expected to strengthen OGX's technology portfolio by expanding into enterprise AI solutions, complementing the company's existing network, cybersecurity and enterprise data centre offerings," it said in a statement.
OGX said the partnership will cover Axtraction AI's core platform offerings, including Investigation Decision AI for law enforcement and regulatory agencies, as well as Finance Operation AI for large enterprises.
Investigation Decision AI is designed to consolidate disparate intelligence streams into a single connected view to support faster analytical and tactical decision-making.
Finance Operation AI, meanwhile, automates critical workflows and transaction validation within enterprise resource planning systems.
OGX executive director and managing director Tan Suan Loong said the partnership strengthens the company's ability to provide practical, enterprise-grade AI solutions to customers as organisations increasingly adopt AI to improve workflow efficiency and decision-making.
He said the partnership also extends OGX's role as an information technology infrastructure solutions specialist by connecting technology providers with Malaysia's enterprise ecosystem.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MACC: Six Felda and FIC cases under investigation, arrests imminent
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has opened six new investigation papers into alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), with several arrests expected beginning next week.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigations followed information received on Aug 24 regarding the implementation of projects and investments by Felda and FIC management between 2010 and 2020.
“We received the information on Aug 24 and, through Ops Fella, the six investigation papers opened involve issues concerning the purchase and investment in assets by Felda and FIC, which are suspected of involving elements of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption,” he told a press conference at the MACC headquarters here today.
The six matters are the purchase of Tataran Aras Sdn Bhd in Limbang, Sarawak; the acquisition of Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd in Sabah; the purchase of Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments in London; the establishment of Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd; the acquisition of Felda House and Grand Felda House; and alleged misappropriation in the development of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.
“MACC is also reviewing an old investigation paper involving the Park City Grand Plaza property, which has yet to be closed and is currently undergoing a mutual legal assistance (MLA) process,” he said.
So far, 12 individuals have had their statements recorded, comprising three FIC board members, an FIC secretary, two FIC Legal Division officers, a valuer, three individuals from law firms, a Kuala Lumpur Land and Mines Office (PTG) officer and an officer from the Kuala Lumpur Valuation and Property Services Department.
Abd Halim said several arrests were expected to be made in stages beginning early next week, while the amount of corruption proceeds believed to be involved had yet to be determined as the investigation was still at an early stage.
He said MACC also received information on Aug 24 from the chairman of the Pertubuhan Badan Bertindak Generasi Palong (Perbagi) regarding concerns over the quality of oil palm seedlings and the implementation of oil palm development and replanting programmes at Felda Palong 7.
He said the information concerned a development programme reportedly benefiting about 450 settlers, including issues related to supply and delivery.
“MACC gives an assurance that its investigation into Felda’s management will be conducted comprehensively, fairly and professionally, based on the principle of the rule of law,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Perak police launch investigations over toddler’s fatal fall at Victoria Bridge
Article:
IPOH, Sept  2 — Police have opened two investigation papers into the death of a three-year-old boy who is believed to have fallen about five metres from Victoria Bridge in Enggor, near Kuala Kangsar, yesterday.
Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation papers were opened under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, with several individuals summoned to assist the investigation.
Based on statements from several witnesses, the victim is believed to have fallen while walking after stepping into a gap in the bridge’s structure.
“Preliminary investigations found no element of negligence in the incident. We are awaiting the post-mortem results from Kuala Kangsar Hospital,” he told a press conference at the Sungai Siput District Police Headquarters (IPD) here today.
Meanwhile, State Housing and Local Government Committee chairperson Sandrea Ng Shy Ching said the Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council (MPKK) had immediately closed visitor access to the steel structure section of the bridge as a safety measure.
She said the closure would remain in place temporarily pending the replacement of worn and rotten track timbers, installation of additional safety measures and confirmation that the area is safe to reopen.
“According to MPKK, the bridge has been monitored periodically, with the latest physical inspection conducted on June 30, 2026.
“Prior to this incident, an application for funds had already been submitted for maintenance work, including the replacement of about 60 worn-out track timbers,” she said in a statement.
Sandrea added that MPKK was also seeking about RM50,000 as an immediate allocation to install safety netting beneath the bridge while awaiting funds for other repair works.
She said the overall safety of the site would also be reviewed in consultation with the relevant parties to determine appropriate improvement measures.
The victim, Abdul Rafee Abdul Halim, reportedly fell through a gap in the bridge at about 6.30 pm yesterday while walking with his father and died in the incident.
The more than 125-year-old Victoria Bridge is a historic railway bridge in Enggor. — Bernama

Title: MACC investigator: Muhyiddin abused powers as PM to help Jana Wibawa contractors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin abused his powers as a prime minister when he acted to help Bumiputera contractors to eventually get government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme, an anti-corruption investigator told the High Court.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) senior assistant commissioner Mazery Mohd Zaini, who was the investigating officer for Muhyiddin’s case, said this while testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in the latter’s power abuse trial.
Mazery said he had also previously investigated Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president and KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd managing director Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff as a suspect in a corruption case.
Mazery confirmed that Azman was not remanded or charged in that case.
Mazery explained that this was because investigations showed that the businessman had given money to Muhyiddin’s Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia after being asked to do so by the then Prime Minister.
“Yes, I investigated this complaint which stated that Datuk Azman Yusoff had asked for and received bribes from companies as a reward for helping those companies receive Jana Wibawa projects,” he told lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin.
“Based on the investigations, it was found there was abuse of power by the prime minister at that time, where he had helped by instructing the finance minister to handle applications by companies,” he said, adding that Azman was then made into a witness instead.
When asked by Wan Shaharuddin to explain why he said Muhyiddin had abused his powers as prime minister, Mazery said this was due to Muhyiddin’s actions in relation to companies who were applying for Jana Wibawa projects.
“Because of his action at that time, instructing the finance minister to help companies who applied and subsequently the companies which were successfully helped made donations. Companies which successfully obtained projects had donated to the party Bersatu,” Mazery said.
Muhyiddin was prime minister from March 1, 2020 until Aug 20, 2021.
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik immediately objected to Mazery’s testimony that claimed his client had abused his powers as prime minister, saying that this should be left to the High Court to conclude.
While Hisyam asked for this part of Mazery’s testimony to be expunged or removed from court records, High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin said it does not have to be expunged as it involved the investigator’s investigations.
Recording Hisyam’s objections, the judge said she will make her own conclusions: “But it’s not binding on the court, I have to make my own finding.”
Golf allowed during Covid-19 lockdown in Malaysia
Previously, Azman as the 27th prosecution witness said he had in July 2020 joined the Tan Sri Muhyiddin Charity Golf (TSMCG) golf tournament at Tropicana Golf Club in the morning, before attending a one-on-one meeting with Muhyiddin at 3pm at the club on the same day.
Azman said Muhyiddin had in the meeting spontaneously told him that contractors could donate directly to Bersatu, and that Muhyiddin had also told him about the Jana Wibawa programme then.
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad had previously challenged Azman’s testimony about the July 2020 golfing event by saying that the TSMCG tournament only took place in October 2020.
Yesterday, Tropicana Golf Club’s security chief Saravanan Subaramaniam told the High Court that the club’s computer system showed that Muhyiddin and 14 other players including an “Azman” had played a golf game there on July 19, 2020.
Today, Mazery said he was informed on July 23, 2026 by his fellow MACC investigator about the exact date of this golf game, namely July 19, 2020.
Mazery told Wan Shaharuddin that he had not received any notice of alibi from Muhyiddin’s lawyers to show where their client was on July 19, 2020.
Mazery confirmed that he had seen Muhyiddin’s May 1, 2020 speech, where the Malaysian government had allowed golf to be played amid the Conditional Movement Control Order (CMCO) during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Mazery read out an excerpt of that speech, where Malaysians were told that outdoor sports such as jogging, cycling, playing golf and running in small groups not exceeding 10 persons were allowed, with the condition that they practise social distancing.
Previously, Muhyiddin’s lawyer Amer had also challenged Azman by saying that sports were not allowed during the Movement Control Order (MCO) in May 2020, but Azman said playing golf while maintaining social distancing was already allowed in May 2020.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial is scheduled to resume tomorrow, with Azman expected to be further cross-examined by Muhyiddin’s lawyers.
