Title: Don’t sacrifice independent oversight for speed in Sabah’s water crisis fixes, says former Water Dept director
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Sabah’s recurring water supply problems require urgent and practical solutions, but the push for faster action should not come at the expense of independent engineering judgement, said Datuk Amarjit Singh.
The former Sabah Water Department director said a clear distinction must be maintained between an engineering consultancy practice and a commercial service provider, particularly when companies supplying water infrastructure, equipment, or specialised technologies are also proposing solutions.
“The issue is not whether service providers have the technical capability to contribute. Many possess valuable operational experience, specialised technology, and the ability to deliver projects quickly. The issue is independence,” he said in a statement.
Amarjit said companies recommending technologies in which they have a commercial interest could face an inherent potential conflict, making independent assessment important.
He pointed out that under Malaysia’s engineering regulatory framework, an Engineering Consultancy Practice registered with the Board of Engineers Malaysia (BEM) has a professional role in providing independent engineering advice, including feasibility assessments, design, and certification within its lawful scope.
“Employing a professional engineer does not by itself make a product manufacturer, operator, or service company an independent engineering consultancy practice,” he said.
Major water supply decisions, including desalination, water reuse, additional storage, leakage reduction, and watershed protection, should begin with an impartial assessment of available options, he said.
Amarjit said companies recommending technologies in which they have a commercial interest could face an inherent potential conflict, making independent assessment important. — The Borneo Post pic
For advanced technologies such as desalination, feasibility studies should consider not only capital costs but also energy consumption, reliability, environmental impacts, waste management, maintenance, replacement costs, and whole-of-life expenditure.
“Consultants should provide independent professional advice and evaluate the available options; service providers should bring proven technologies, specialist knowledge, implementation capability and operational support,” he said.
Amarjit stressed he is not arguing against service providers, but calling for their expertise to complement independent engineering advice.
“The party selling or operating a solution should not be the sole party deciding that the same solution is the best one for the public,” he said.
He called for major water projects to undergo independent engineering assessment before commitments are made, saying this would strengthen procurement decisions and ensure Sabah’s resources are directed towards solutions that are technically sound, environmentally responsible, and financially sustainable.
“Sabah’s water future deserves decisions based on evidence rather than on the attractiveness of a packaged solution. Speed is important but so are transparency, accountability, and professional independence,” he said.
Amarjit added that his comments were intended to contribute to public discussion on infrastructure governance and water security and were not directed at or intended to allege wrongdoing by any particular company or organisation. — The Borneo Post

Title: Batik Air agrees to resume Miri-KL flights after deputy minister’s request
Article:
MIRI, Sept 2 — Batik Air has agreed to resume its Miri-Kuala Lumpur services following a formal request by Deputy Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture Chiew Choon Man.
The Miri MP said the commencement date, flight frequency and schedule would be announced by the airline in due course.
Chiew said he had received increasing feedback from Miri residents over the difficulty of securing flights between Miri and Kuala Lumpur, particularly during weekends, public holidays and peak travel periods.
“Flights are often heavily booked, and airfares can become very expensive when seat availability is limited,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said he had formally written to Batik Air’s chief executive officer Datuk Chandran Rama Muthy, urging the airline to review the commercial viability of the Miri-Kuala Lumpur sector and consider returning to Miri.
Chiew said current market conditions should be reassessed, noting that while the airline’s previous operations had been affected by challenges such as volatility in fuel and aviation costs, demand for travel between Miri and Kuala Lumpur remained strong.
He also stressed that Miri’s potential should not be assessed based solely on the city’s population, as it serves a wider catchment area encompassing northern Sarawak and neighbouring Brunei Darussalam.
“With suitable flight timings and competitive fares, there is further potential to attract Bruneian passengers who use Miri as an alternative gateway to Kuala Lumpur and onward destinations,” he said.
Chiew welcomed Batik Air’s positive response, describing the return of another airline operator as important for Miri.
He said additional capacity would give passengers more choices, improve connectivity and help ease pressure on seat availability during periods of strong demand.
“Greater competition and additional capacity can also contribute towards a healthier and more competitive airfare environment for travellers.
“Improved air connectivity is also important for Miri’s wider economic and tourism development,” he said.
Chiew said in his capacity as Miri MP and deputy minister, he would continue working with airlines and relevant stakeholders to strengthen Miri’s connectivity.
He added that his office was prepared to support Batik Air in developing the route, including facilitating engagement with tourism industry players, travel agents, business associations and other relevant stakeholders in Miri and Brunei.
He also thanked Batik Air Malaysia’s management for listening to the concerns and needs of Miri residents and responding positively to the request. — The Borneo Post

Title: US embassy shifts Sabah travel status to ‘relaxed’ after security improvements
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — The United States is encouraging its citizens and international travellers to visit Sabah, citing significant improvements in security and a corresponding relaxation of travel advisories, said US Embassy Kuala Lumpur Chargé d'Affaires David Gamble.
He noted that the US lowered its travel advisory for Sabah and Borneo earlier this year, a move that has prompted several other nations to review their own warnings.
“Now it is at a very relaxed travel status. Many countries are following America’s lead and reviewing their travel advisories as well,” Gamble said during the launch of the Freedom 250 Sabah programme at the Tanjung Aru State Library today.
“This reflects the improved security and how safe it is to visit Sabah. We want to encourage more tourists to visit Sabah because Sabah is a wonderful place to visit.”
The shift follows a period of heightened caution that began in July 2014 after a series of kidnapping-for-ransom incidents along the east coast.
In February, the US Embassy downgraded its advisory for Eastern Sabah to Level 1, advising citizens to exercise only normal precautions, though maritime areas and offshore islands remain at Level 2. Japan has similarly lowered its advisory for coastal areas from Kudat to Tawau to Level 1.
When asked about the possibility of establishing a US consulate in Kota Kinabalu, Gamble clarified that there are no plans to do so in the coming years.
The diplomatic push coincides with "Freedom 250," a three-day series of events in Kota Kinabalu commemorating the 250th anniversary of American independence. The programme celebrates the longstanding ties between the US and Sabah through education, culture, sports, and people-to-people exchanges.
Highlights of the celebration include the travelling Freedom 250 Exhibition at the Tanjung Aru State Library, STEM workshops supported by McDermott and ConocoPhillips, and the English Access Scholarship Programme. In the sporting arena, three-time Olympic gold medallist Shannon Boxx is leading a football clinic for up to 500 young Sabahan athletes.
The festivities will culminate tomorrow with the Great American Sabah State Fair and Freedom 250 Fun Run at Padang Merdeka from 3pm to 10pm. The fair will feature American-inspired cuisine, local vendors, and a live performance by the US Pacific Band. Additionally, American cinematic classics such as “Back to the Future” and “The Incredibles” will be screened at City Cineplex, City Mall.
These celebrations run parallel to the 22nd Pacific Partnership mission in Sabah, where approximately 400 US service members and personnel from eight partner nations, including the UK, Japan, and Australia, are collaborating with local communities on engineering projects, medical outreach, and disaster preparedness.
Gamble noted that these diverse programmes reflect the breadth of the US-Sabah relationship, providing young Sabahans with direct access to American innovation, education, and culture.

Title: Retiree loses RM1.417m after transferring savings across multiple accounts in phone‑call scam
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 2 — A retiree of a national multinational oil and gas company suffered a loss of RM1.417 million after being duped by a telephone fraud syndicate between May and yesterday.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 66-year-old man, received a call from an unknown individual on May 19 who claimed that the victim was involved in money laundering activities.
He said the victim was then instructed to open an Agrobank account and transfer his savings to the account for the purpose of checking by the authorities.
“After opening the account, a man came to meet the victim in his residential area and the victim handed over his bank card and PIN number to the man,” he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, he said the victim had also transferred money from his Employees Provident Fund (EPF), Amanah Saham Berhad and Tabung Haji accounts as well as pawn gold proceeds totalling RM1,417,210 to the Agrobank account as of yesterday.
Azry Akmar said the victim then realised that the money in the account had been transferred to six different accounts and withdrawn via an automated teller machine (ATM) without his knowledge.
He advised the public to seek advice from the nearest police station before taking any action after receiving a suspicious call to avoid becoming a victim of fraud.
“The public is also advised to check the account number via the Semak Mule website before making any transaction and to contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 if they are a victim of fraud,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: One teen found dead as search continues for three others missing in Tanjung Balau
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The body of one of four teenagers feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach in Tanjung Balau was recovered this afternoon.
The victim, identified as Alif Taqiudin Kamal Hasrul Mohamad, was found by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 1.25pm, approximately 800 metres from the location where he was last seen.
Kota Tinggi police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed that the body was identified by family members and has since been transported to Kota Tinggi Hospital.
“The SAR operation for the other three victims is still ongoing,” he told reporters today.
The tragedy unfolded at 7.45am this morning when a group of 15 teenagers, camping in conjunction with the school holidays, encountered distress in the water.
While six of them drowned, two 16-year-old students — identified as Mohamad Faqrul Islander Abdullah and Muhammad Afiq Ruzaini Mazlan — were successfully rescued. Four others remain missing.
Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Soleh Nasir noted that the rescue efforts have been severely hampered by strong undersea currents, rough beach conditions, and high winds.
“We are using the surface searching technique in this SAR operation,” he stated.
A massive coordination effort is currently underway, involving 30 personnel from the police, the Fire and Rescue Department, marine police, and the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA). They are being supported by the Tanjung Balau Fishermen's Association and local sailors.

Title: Johor dengue cases jump 131pc to 9,954 as infections rise across districts
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 2 — Johor recorded 9,954 dengue cases as of Epid Week (ME) 34 this year, an increase of 131.3 per cent compared to 4,304 cases for the same period last year.
State Health and Environment Committee Chairman Ling Tian Soon said of the total, 4,520 cases or 45.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities while 5,434 cases or 54.6 per cent were from non-outbreak localities.
He said for ME34 alone, a total of 664 dengue fever cases were reported, an increase of two per cent compared to 651 cases in the previous week.
“Of the total dengue cases reported throughout ME34, 308 cases or 46.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities and 356 cases or 53.6 per cent from non-outbreak localities,” he said in a statement today.
Ling said Johor Bahru recorded the highest number of cases in the week in question with 495 cases or 74.6 per cent of the total cases, followed by Kulai (120), Batu Pahat (19), Segamat (nine), Kota Tinggi (seven), Muar and Pontian with four cases each.
Meanwhile, a total of 13 deaths due to dengue were recorded up to ME33 this year compared to eight deaths for the same period in 2025, an increase of 62.5 per cent.
He said a total of 3,745 compounds with a total value of RM1.87 million were issued through enforcement activities throughout the year with 80.2 per cent of them paid. — Bernama

Title: MMEA detains tugboat and dredger over suspected ship‑to‑ship transfer; RM260m oil cargo seized off Tanjung Buai
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) detained two vessels suspected of carrying out unauthorised ship-to-ship activities in national waters early yesterday morning, with the value of the seized goods estimated at RM260 million.
Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime acting director Maritime Commander Mohd Najib Sam said the action was carried out at 3.20am after receiving public information regarding two suspicious vessels seen huddled together at a position about 1.4 nautical miles northwest of Tanjung Buai.
“Further inspection also found a quantity of oil cargo believed to have no documents relating to ownership and delivery.
The two vessels, consisting of a tugboat and a dredger, each registered in Malaysia, along with the oil cargo, have been detained for further investigation,” he said.
Mohd Najib said the tugboat was operated by a crew of five including the skipper, consisting of local and Indonesian citizens aged between 26 and 58 years, while the dredger was operated by a crew of 13 including the skipper, all local citizens aged between 22 and 51 years.
The case is being investigated under Section 491B(1)(K) of the Merchant Shipping Ordinance (OPS) 1952 for suspected ship-to-ship activities without the permission of the Malaysian Director of Marine.
The case is also being investigated under Section 491B(1)(L) of the OPS 1952 for anchoring without permission and the Customs Act 1967 regarding the discovery of a cargo of oil suspected of not having the relevant documents. — Bernama

Title: VIPs and officials in crosshairs as MACC readies charges for multiple suspects in TH probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is moving to charge several individuals over the next two days following a massive probe into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH).
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said that the upcoming charges centre on the alleged abuse of power and misappropriation of RM334.2 million linked to investments in TH Marine, TH Alam, and TH Alam Management,
FMT
reported.
“Another charge involves alleged corruption related to TH’s 30 per cent stake in construction company Putrajaya Perdana Bhd. Once the cases are registered, we will know the details. At this point, I cannot say more,” Halim told a press conference at the MACC headquarters today.
The suspects are expected to be produced before the Kuala Lumpur and Shah Alam Sessions Courts.
In a parallel development, Halim disclosed that a separate investigation into TH’s investment in Al-Rawda Real Estate Development and Project Management Company Ltd is nearing completion.
The case involves hotel leases in Mecca and Medina valued at approximately RM2.68 billion and is expected to result in charges next week.
“Yes, the charges involve a VIP,” Halim confirmed.
The scale of the losses was previously detailed by Finance Minister II Amir Hamzah Azizan during a special Dewan Rakyat sitting on Aug 11.
Amir noted that the RCI into TH’s financial management from 2014 to 2020 found that seven of the fund’s 14 investments resulted in losses, with the Al-Rawda deal being the most severe.
Between 2015 and 2017, TH paid 1.4 billion Saudi riyals (approximately RM1.5 billion) to an intermediary to lease four hotels in Mecca and Medina for Malaysian pilgrims.
While Al-Rawda was contracted to operate the hotels and repay TH 2.49 billion Saudi riyals in rental, the company defaulted starting in the first quarter of 2019. Because the investment was secured only through personal promissory notes, TH was forced to recognise a full impairment loss of RM1 billion in 2024.
The crackdown has already seen significant arrests. Earlier today, a former minister was remanded for five days to assist in the Al-Rawda probe.
A total of 11 other individuals have also been detained, including a former TH chairman (60), a former managing director (61), and three former senior general managers.
Other detainees include a former minister (65), a director of Putrajaya Perdana Bhd (59), a former director of the same firm (69), a former director of Putra Perdana Construction Sdn Bhd (61), and the chief operating officer of Alam Maritim Sdn Bhd (67).

Title: Man remanded after viral video of provocative act at National Day celebration in Putrajaya
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A man in his 30s, believed to be involved in a provocative incident during the 69th National Day celebrations last Monday, has been remanded for one day starting today.
Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah issued the remand order following an application by the police.
Putrajaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed confirmed the arrest when contacted. “The suspect has been remanded for one day starting today,” he said.
Prior to this, a video went viral on social media showing a man acting provocatively by attempting to jump over a barrier to enter the seating area during the 69th National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya.
The case is being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955. — Bernama

Title: Hannah Yeoh’s official website confirms divorce after 18-year marriage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and her husband Ramachandran Muniandy have divorced after 18 years of marriage.
Yeoh’s official website states that she married Ramachandran in 2008, shortly before running for public office, and that they have two children, Shay and Kayleigh.
According to the website, their children were born in 2011 and 2013, and the couple divorced in 2026 after 18 years of marriage.
Yeoh is the Segambut Member of Parliament, a seat she first won in the 2018 general election.
She previously served as a two-term Subang Jaya state assemblywoman from 2008 to 2018 and became the first woman to be elected Speaker of the Selangor State Legislative Assembly in 2013.
She was appointed Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister in 2018, serving until 2020, before becoming Youth and Sports Minister from 2022 to 2025.
Yeoh was later appointed Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) in December 2025.
Within DAP, Yeoh currently serves as deputy secretary-general, vice-chair of DAP and a committee member of DAP Wanita.

Title: ‘Not a coincidence’: Contractors’ RM25.3m to Bersatu came after Muhyiddin’s aid to get projects, was not ‘political donation’, court told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The RM25.3 million that three Bumiputera contractors and their representatives had given to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia in 2021 and 2022 is not a “political donation”, an anti-corruption investigator told the High Court today.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigating officer Mazery Mohd Zaini said the RM25.3 million was instead a reward given after Bersatu president and former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin helped these companies get government projects.
“The investigation also found that the money deposited from these companies are not a political donation, instead it is a ‘
balasan
’ (reward) for the accused’s actions which helped them get those projects,” the MACC senior assistant commissioner told the High Court, referring to Muhyiddin as the accused.
Mazery said this while testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s abuse‑of‑power and money‑laundering trial.
Mazery repeatedly stressed that the RM25.3 million paid out by these companies to Bersatu was “not a coincidence”, as they had all made the payments after obtaining the government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme.
Previously, the High Court had heard from other prosecution witnesses that KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd and its managing director Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff gave RM4.8 million to Bersatu after getting a project, while Nepturis Sdn Bhd had given RM1 million after also getting a project.
The High Court also previously heard that Mamfor Sdn Bhd gave RM19.5 million to Bersatu after its director’s younger brother’s company, Sutracom Sdn Bhd, won a project, with Mazery saying that RM10 million of this RM19.5 million was paid out before the contract award document (SST) was issued as Sutracom found out via Azman that the project award had been approved.
Mazery said Muhyiddin was one of the authorised signatories for Bersatu’s CIMB and AmBank bank accounts that received the RM25.3 million, explaining that an authorised signatory could control any transactions in the account including receiving, using and withdrawing funds.
Mazery said the RM25.3 million was not a genuine donation.
Mazery pointed out it might have been different if these companies had donated to Bersatu despite not receiving any government projects, or if the companies had donated before applying for the projects, and if the donations were in smaller and more reasonable sums.
In his investigations, Mazery said he did not find any donation receipts issued by Bersatu for the RM25.3 million given by KCJ Engineering, Azman, Nepturis, and Mamfor.
Mazery said there was no reason for witnesses from these companies to fabricate their testimony against Muhyiddin, and noted that their testimony were all backed by documents.
“The most important fact that I found is that all project application letters were sent to the accused, and secondly, money was only deposited into the party Bersatu’s account,” he said.
Mazery said Muhyiddin had written “minutes” or notes that enabled both Nepturis and Sutracom to obtain the Jana Wibawa projects through pre-qualification tenders, citing the “minutes” where he had agreed that the projects that they were bidding for should be done through such tenders.
Mazery also said that Muhyiddin had listed KCJ Engineering as one of 54 contractors in his November 13, 2020, proposal to the Finance Ministry for appointment for 54 Jana Wibawa projects through direct negotiation.
While it is still up to the Finance Ministry and Public Works Department to evaluate contractors and to approve the awarding of the Jana Wibawa projects, Mazery said Muhyiddin’s actions had “opened the path” for the three companies to be considered for those projects.
Without Muhyiddin’s minutes and November 13, 2020 letter, the Finance Ministry would not have started the process to consider those contractors for the projects, Mazery said.
Mazery also said the contractors’ owners and representatives have said they would not have given money to Bersatu if they did not get the Jana Wibawa projects.
Mazery said the MACC had recorded Muhyiddin’s testimony as part of its investigations in this case, but noted that the former prime minister did not disclose various matters during the investigation, including:
that these companies had given money to Bersatu after the government projects were approved;
what happened on July 19, 2020, between him and Azman.
why he had asked contractors who obtained Jana Wibawa projects to donate to Bersatu;
how he obtained the list of 54 companies including KCJ Engineering.
Previously, Azman said he had a July 2020 one-on-one meeting with Muhyiddin on opportunites for Bumiputera contractors to get government projects, where the then-prime minister spontaneously said contractors could donate directly to Bersatu and also spoke about the Jana Wibawa programme.
Among other things, Mazery said Muhyiddin had never disclosed to anyone that Bersatu had received the RM25.3 million from the three companies and Azman.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume tomorrow, with Azman expected to be further cross-examined.

Title: Sabah activates state and district disaster command centres as API readings rise to unhealthy levels
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Sabah has activated its State Disaster Operations Command Centre (PKOB), as well as district-level PKOBs in Kota Kinabalu, Keningau and Papar, as the Air Pollutant Index (API) rose yesterday.
State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, who is also State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) chairman, said that API readings reached worrying unhealthy levels yesterday in Kota Kinabalu (177), Tawau (153), Keningau (165), Kimanis, Papar (166) and Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic (153).
“Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor was informed today that the increase in API readings was influenced by wind movement towards Sabah and was expected to continue rising steadily as long as there was no rain in Kalimantan,” he said.
Based on the National Haze Action Plan, the API readings were all categorised under Alert Level 1A, which prescribed measures such as suspending activities outside classrooms, postponing co-curricular and sports activities, informing the public of API readings and precautionary measures, stepping up enforcement and intensifying monitoring of industries and landfill sites.
Zainudin said a haze emergency or disaster would be declared when API readings reached 500 and above.
He suggested that official State government activities be cancelled or postponed if the API reading reaches or exceeds 200, although indoor activities would still be allowed.
Zainudin also recommended that schools in areas where the API reading reaches or exceeds 200 be closed and switch to learning from home.
“It is proposed that
solat hajat
be held in every district for Muslims as part of efforts to seek protection and well-being.”
“At the same time, houses of worship of other religions are also encouraged to hold appropriate religious activities in accordance with their respective beliefs and practices,” he said.

Title: PPC orders formation of special task force to probe Penang ferry-cargo vessel collision
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 2 — Authorities have ordered the formation of a special task force to investigate last night’s collision between the Teluk Bahang Ferry and cargo vessel MV Mekar Jaya in Penang Port waters.
Penang Port Commission (PPC) Chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said the task force would investigate the cause of the incident and determine the circumstances surrounding the collision.
“I immediately instructed the PPC and ferry operator Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB) to set up a special task force to thoroughly probe the cause of the accident in an objective, transparent and professional manner, establish the facts, and report fully to the public,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Yeoh said relevant parties have also been instructed to gather information and assist with compensation matters.
He said he went to the ferry terminal in Butterworth shortly after the collision to assess the situation and be briefed before visiting the injured at the hospital.
Yeoh said the operator had also been instructed to review its operational procedures and safety mechanisms, with further action to be taken based on the investigation findings.
“We will not avoid any issues and will take the necessary follow-up action and improve measures to prevent similar incidents from happening again,” he said.
He said the PPC would continue to work closely with PPSB and relevant parties to implement all follow-up measures, while ensuring ferry services continue to operate as usual.
Meanwhile, Penang Youth, Sports and Health Committee chairman Daniel Gooi Zi Sen, when contacted, said none of the victims had been admitted to hospital.
He said 21 people were reported injured, and eleven of them were taken by ambulance to Seberang Jaya Hospital.
Ten others with minor injuries initially said they would make their own way there, but only seven eventually turned up at the hospital later.
Gooi said the 18 injured were given outpatient treatment at the hospital’s Emergency Department, adding that no other victims had sought treatment at other government health facilities so far.
The collision occurred at 8.40 pm yesterday when the Teluk Bahang Ferry, which was heading towards the Sultan Abdul Halim Ferry Terminal, collided with MV Mekar Jaya within Penang Port limits.
MV Mekar Jaya was reported to be travelling from the Butterworth Deep Water Wharves to the Swettenham Pier Cruise Terminal. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji RCI: Former minister remanded five days in Saudi Arabia hotel lease probe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A former minister has been remanded for five days to assist investigations into a hotel lease issue involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) in Saudi Arabia.
The remand order, which runs from today until Sunday, was issued against the individual, who is in his 60s, by Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Magistrate’s Court here today.
The former minister was arrested at about 4.30pm yesterday when he appeared at the MACC to have his statement recorded.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case was being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on TH was made public on July 29, documenting various weaknesses in TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, as well as listing problematic investments requiring a forensic audit.
The report also stated that there were suspicious transactions and concealment of information. — Bernama

Title: Ambulance driver charged with reckless driving over fatal Jasin crash pleads not guilty
Article:
JASIN, Sept 2 — An ambulance driver pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate’s Court here today to a charge of reckless driving that resulted in the death of an 18-year-old motorcyclist last week.
Mohd Noorikhmal Baharuddin, 41, was charged under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act with driving a Toyota Hiace ambulance recklessly at the Kampung Ayer Merbau T-junction traffic light at about 9.15 am on Aug 26, causing the death of Muhammad Amirul Asyraaf Md Azizan.
The offence carries a jail term of five to 10 years, a fine of RM20,000 to RM50,000, and disqualification from holding a driving licence for up to five years.
The prosecution, conducted by Prosecuting Officer Inspector Mohd Hafiz Othman, proposed RM8,000 bail with one surety and a temporary suspension of the accused’s driving licence. Defence counsel Datin Kharen Jit Kaur sought lower bail, citing his cooperation with the investigation.
Magistrate Mazana Sinin set bail at RM3,000 and allowed the additional condition on his driving licence. She also set Sept 17 for mention for the submission of relevant documents. — Bernama

Title: Prime Minister’s Department blocks airing of ‘Madu atau Racun’ over religious‑sensitivity concerns
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Prime Minister’s Department (JPM) has rejected the airing of the drama
Madu atau Racun
, which has allegedly sparked public concern and controversy.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Zulkifli Hasan expressed regret over the inclusion of elements that touched on religious sensitivities and local cultural norms, whether explicitly or implicitly.
“The inclusion of elements contrary to Islamic teachings and Eastern cultural values must be curbed to ensure that the faith and moral values of the community, particularly the young generation, remain safeguarded,” he said in a statement today.
He said Islamic principles uphold the sanctity of the family institution and the decorum of religious life, while depictions of deviant lifestyles are contrary to these noble values.
In this regard, Zulkifli said the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) would work closely with relevant agencies to review the content and take appropriate follow-up action based on the Guidelines for Content Screening of Islamic-Themed Broadcasting Materials (Jakim No. 4/2015) and existing legal provisions.
He said the measure was important to ensure that all broadcast content was appropriate and upheld the sanctity of the religion.
Meanwhile, Zulkifli urged creative industry practitioners, producers and broadcasters to remain sensitive and responsible by referring to established official guidelines when producing works that nurture positive values and contribute to nation-building.
“The arts industry and media platforms should be utilised as mediums to instil virtuous values, rather than to spark controversies that could undermine the harmony of societal norms,” he said.
He also called on the Muslim community to unite in upholding the sanctity of the religion and moral integrity with steadfastness and wisdom. — Bernama

Title: Kelantan’s Nik Mohamad Abduh begins second Senate term after taking oath of office
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Former Bachok MP Nik Mohamad Abduh Nik Abdul Aziz took his oath of office as a senator for a second term today before Dewan Negara President Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah at the Senate chamber in Parliament.
Nik Mohamad Abduh was re-elected by the Kelantan State Legislative Assembly under Article 45(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution for a three-year term, effective from July 7, 2026, to July 6, 2029.
The son of the late Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Nik Abdul Aziz Nik Mat had previously served as a senator representing Kelantan for his first term from July 8, 2023, to July 7 this year, and has also served as MP for Pasir Mas and Bachok.
In his proclamation speech, Awang Bemee said the re-election reflected the continued confidence and trust in Nik Mohamad Abduh’s credibility, experience and ability to contribute meaningfully to parliamentary proceedings and the broader functioning of the institution.
He said the oath of a senator entails a solemn duty to uphold the Constitution, champion the welfare of the people and guarantee that the voices of all states are afforded their rightful place.
He said Nik Mohamad Abduh’s track record from his first Senate term would be leveraged to strengthen the institution’s functions, represent Kelantan’s interests as well as scrutinise national policies and legislation.
Meanwhile, Awang Bemee affirmed Parliament’s commitment to further enhance the country’s legislative institution, including through the enforcement of the Parliamentary Service Act.
He said such measures are crucial for reinforcing the principle of separation of powers, improving checks and balances, and bolstering Parliament’s autonomy and standing.
“Indeed, a strong Parliament strengthens democracy, and a strong democracy leads to more accountable governance,” he said.
According to the parliamentary calendar, the Senate sitting for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Term of the 15th Parliament will run for 14 days, beginning November 30. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Fire Dept: Missing 11‑year‑old girl found drowned in Sungai Bengkoka after search launched for five victims
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — An 11-year-old girl who was reported missing in Sungai Bengkoka, Pitas, yesterday afternoon was found drowned this morning.
Pitas Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) chief Noor Jali Maslah, in a statement today, said the victim was found by villagers at 7.36am, about one kilometre from the Fire and Rescue Control Centre (PKB).
He said firefighters then retrieved the victim using a stretcher before handing her body to the police.
Noor Jali said the search and rescue (SAR) operation was launched after the station received an emergency call at 5.17pm yesterday regarding an incident involving five victims in the river.
He said six personnel from BBP Pitas conducted the operation using a National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) boat, employing the Surface Water Rescue method within a one-kilometre search radius from the PKB.
In the incident, two girls, aged four and 14, nearly drowned and were sent to hospital, while an 18-year-old woman and a 14-year-old boy were safe. — Bernama

Title: Fire Dept launches search after four teenage boys feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach in Johor
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — Four 16-year-old boys are feared to have drowned while swimming at Tanjung Lompat Beach, Tanjung Balau, Penawar, this morning.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said it received an emergency call at 8.19am, after which six personnel from the Bandar Penawar Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the scene.
“Initial information from members of the public indicated that six victims had got into difficulties while swimming at the beach.
“Two of the victims were rescued by members of the public at 7.45am before the Operations Response Team arrived at the scene,” the statement said.
The statement identified the missing teens as Alif Taqiudin, Mohd Haiman, Adib Rizqi and Thaqif Rayyan.
It is understood that all four were part of a group of 15 teenagers who had gone camping in the area since 6.30 pm yesterday.
A search-and-rescue operation has been launched. — Bernama

Title: Samarahan moves out of hazardous category as Sarawak haze eases slightly
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 2 — Samarahan moved out of the Hazardous air quality category this morning after its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading fell from 302 at 8am to 292 at 10am.
The latest reading placed Samarahan in the Very Unhealthy category, marking one of the more notable improvements recorded across Sarawak on Wednesday morning.
According to the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) Sarawak’s Daily Haze Watch, most monitoring stations also recorded lower API readings by 10am compared with 8am, indicating a gradual improvement in air quality across the state.
Lubok Antu recorded the highest API reading at 331, down from 335 at 8am, while Lundu fell from 346 to 325, and IPD Serian from 320 to 309.
Kanowit remained unchanged at 323, while Kuching’s API reading stayed at 318.
Among stations in the Very Unhealthy category, Sarikei improved from 283 to 275, Sibu from 292 to 284, Tebedu from 279 to 270, and Mukah from 241 to 232.
Bintulu also recorded a slight improvement, with its API falling from 226 to 223, while Sri Aman dropped from 214 to 211.
Meanwhile, Miri improved from 181 to 178 and Betong from 194 to 192. Bario recorded a decrease from 157 to 150.
However, several stations recorded marginal increases, including Limbang from 173 to 174, Lawas from 182 to 186 and Kapit from 187 to 188.
As of 10am, five stations remained in the Hazardous category — Lubok Antu (331), Lundu (325), Kanowit (323), Kuching (318), and IPD Serian (309).
Despite the gradual improvement, members of the public in affected areas are advised to continue taking precautions, including limiting outdoor activities, avoiding strenuous physical exertion and wearing suitable protective masks when outdoors. —  The Borneo Post

Title: Alleged provocateur arrested for inciting crowd crush at National Day parade in Putrajaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — A 30-year-old cook has been arrested for allegedly inciting a crowd to breach security barriers to secure seats during the National Day 2026 celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya.
The suspect was detained in Putrajaya yesterday afternoon after five police reports were lodged against him for instigating members of the public to push through the gates early on Aug 31,
NST
reported.
The resulting surge caused a chaotic crush near the perimeter barriers, leaving several spectators injured after being knocked to the ground.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus confirmed the arrest, adding that investigators will apply for a remand order against the suspect today.
"Yes, we have arrested the man in the orange shirt for further investigation under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955," he said today.
The arrest came after a two-minute-and-18-second video clip went viral on Facebook, showing an individual in an orange and brown shirt aggressively agitating the crowd waiting at the seating entrance at around 5am, triggering the barrier breach.
Fadil urged members of the public with information or video footage of the incident to step forward to assist investigators, requesting those involved to report to the Putrajaya district police headquarters.

Title: Six areas in Sabah record unhealthy API readings with KK Polytechnic highest at 185
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Six areas in Sabah recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8 am today, with the Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic station recording the highest reading at 185.
According to the Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) daily El Nino Monitoring infographic report, Kota Kinabalu recorded an API reading of 179, followed by Kimanis at 175, Keningau at 173, Sandakan at 152 and Tawau at 123.
The report stated that API readings between 101 and 200 are categorised as unhealthy, with the public advised to reduce outdoor activities, while children, senior citizens and those with chronic illnesses are advised to avoid outdoor activities.
The report also recorded six fire incidents in the 24-hour period up to 8 am today, comprising five bush or grass fires and one farm or plantation fire, while no forest, peatland or rubbish fires were reported.
Monitoring of rivers showed that Sungai Moyong in Penampang and Sungai Kalabakan in Tawau were both at normal levels. — Bernama

Title: MACC seeks to remand ex-minister over Tabung Haji Saudi Arabia hotel issue
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A former minister arrived at the Magistrate’s Court here today for remand proceedings in connection with investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on Tabung Haji (TH).
The man, in his 60s, arrived at 10.25 am wearing an orange Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) remand shirt.
The individual was arrested at about 4.30 pm yesterday while he was at the MACC headquarters to have his statement recorded, believed to be in connection with investigations into a hotel lease issue involving TH in Saudi Arabia.
The TH RCI report was made public on July 29, documenting various weaknesses in TH’s management and operations between 2014 and 2020, as well as listing problematic investments requiring a forensic audit.
The report also stated that there were suspicious transactions and concealment of information. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian Embassy in Doha issues advisory following US-Iran strikes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Embassy in Doha has advised Malaysians in Qatar to stay abreast of developments and any notices issued by the Qatari authorities following the latest developments in the region.
The embassy, in a notice posted on Facebook, also reminded individuals travelling from or transiting through Qatar to check the latest flight schedules to ensure a smooth journey.
Malaysians requiring further assistance can contact the embassy at +974 3374 6733 / +974 4483 6463 or via email at mwdoha@kln.gov.my.
According to international media reports, the United States (US) launched its latest strikes on Iran on Tuesday, followed by retaliatory attacks by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) against US bases and assets in the region, further escalating tensions in West Asia. — Bernama

Title: Night closures on Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway in Penang from Sept 7 to 9
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 2 — The George Town-bound stretch of the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway will undergo temporary nightly closures and traffic diversions from Sept 7 to 9 to facilitate ongoing highway construction works.
The developer of The Light Waterfront Penang, IJM Land Berhad, announced that the closures will take effect from 10pm to 5am daily along the section from the Jalan Tunku Kudin junction to Jalan Ahmad Nor.
The temporary disruption is to allow for the construction of an elevated U-turn facility, which is designed to complement the upcoming Air Itam Bypass and ease overall traffic congestion along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway.
Motorists travelling towards George Town during these hours are advised to plan their journeys in advance, adhere strictly to on-site directional traffic signage, and drive with caution when approaching the construction zone to ensure public safety.

Title: Malaysia hosts Asean health ministers’ meet again after 20 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Malaysia will play host to the 17th Asean Health Ministers’ Meeting and Related Meetings (AHMM) scheduled to take place from Sept 7 to 11.
The Ministry of Health (MOH), in a Facebook post, said the health meeting will carry the theme, ‘Healthy Asean: Together Towards Equitable, Future-Ready Health Systems.’
“Let us together support efforts towards a more equitable, resilient, and future-ready Asean health system,” the post read.
Malaysia last hosted this prestigious conference two decades ago, during the 7th AHMM in Penang in 2004.
The conference serves as a vital platform for strengthening public health cooperation and addressing regional health challenges holistically. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak haze persists: Serian, Kuching, Samarahan in ‘Hazardous’ zone
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Three areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at hazardous levels as of 8 am today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters (IPD) recording the highest reading at 320.
Based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), the other two areas with hazardous API levels were Kuching (318) and Samarahan (302).
Meanwhile, five areas in Sarawak recorded API readings of very unhealthy levels, namely Sibu (292), Sarikei (283), Mukah (241), Bintulu (226), and Sri Aman (214).
A total of 16 stations recorded API readings at the unhealthy level, with Samalaju, Sarawak, recording the highest reading at 196, followed by Kapit, Sarawak (187), Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic, Sabah (185), ILP Miri, Sarawak (183), and Labuan (181).
Also recording unhealthy readings were Miri, Sarawak (181), Kota Kinabalu, Sabah (179), Kimanis, Sabah (175), Keningau, Sabah (173), Limbang, Sarawak (173), Johan Setia, Selangor (161), Sandakan, Sabah (152), Putrajaya (148), Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (137), Tawau, Sabah (123), and Seremban, Negeri Sembilan (116).
Meanwhile, 44 stations recorded readings at moderate levels.
API readings of 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings exceeding 300 are hazardous. — Bernama
